# Overview {.unnumbered}

This Quarto project is the 2026 restructuring of the analyses behind
*"Running to a standstill: how responsive have successive ONS life
expectancy forecasts been to stalling life expectancy gains?"*, originally
developed in 2019--2020 as a single large R Markdown notebook
(`markdown/bayes_factor_ons_e0.Rmd`, preserved on the `old/pre-refactor`
branch).

The core question: ONS life expectancy forecasts systematically
*under*-projected gains through the 2000s [@white2002longevity;
@oeppen2002broken] and then systematically *over*-projected them after
improvement rates stalled around 2010. How quickly did successive biennial
forecast rounds adapt, and what improvement-rate assumption does the
accumulated evidence actually support?

The analysis proceeds in five chapters:

1. **International trends** --- annual changes in period life expectancy at
   birth ($e_0$) across high-income countries (HMD data [@hmd]), placing the
   UK slowdown in context.
2. **UK trends and breakpoints** --- $e_0$ trends within UK nations, and
   changepoint/segmented-regression analysis [@muggeo2008segmented;
   @killick2014changepoint] locating the break in improvement rates.
3. **ONS projections** --- five decades of projection rounds against
   observed $e_0$ [@ons_npp_accuracy; @ons_expectation_of_life], including
   the 2020-based interim, 2022-based and 2024-based rounds.
4. **Bayes factors** --- likelihood ratios [@kass1995bayes] for 101
   candidate slowdown scenarios (0--100% of the 1991--2010 mean improvement
   rate) against the no-slowdown null, updated as each year of data accrues.
5. **Bayes factors vs ONS assumptions** --- each projection round converted
   to an implied slowdown scenario and scored on the same schedule.

Data provenance, known issues and running findings are logged in
`NOTES.md`. Actual $e_0$ series combine ONS single-year life tables
(1980--2018/2020) [@ons_single_year_lifetables] with historic estimates
embedded in the 2024-based NPP release (2019--2024); the last point is the
projection base year (mid-2024) and is part-estimated.
